_about: Chapter 2: the Lobby (scripts/levels/lobby.gd, docs/CHAPTER2.md). The superintendent's conversation branches on approach and leaves Game.rel.super; Socko's guide lines and his suggestions (obey/defy) follow.

super_hello.text: Come here. Into the light, where I can see you.
Nobody comes in through there. Nobody comes in at all. So which flat are you visiting?

choices.text: Sorry. Didn't mean to barge in. I'm just trying to get upstairs.

steps.text: Polite. I like polite. Polite people sign the book.

choices.text: I'm looking for a way up. Is the lift working?

steps.text: No. Nothing works. That's why they pay me.
You'll sign the book first. Everybody signs the book.

choices.text: Who are you? The super doesn't sit here naked in the dark.

steps.text: Twenty-two years. Every pipe, every fuse, every key. Who are you?

choices.text: Put some clothes on and get out of my way.

steps.text: Nothing in here is your way. The stairs are mine. The doors are mine. The light you're standing in is mine.

choices.text: Housing committee. I'm here about the lift.

steps.text: They never come. Three years I wrote to them about that lift.
Well. The committee signs the book like everybody else.

super_hello.text: Psst. Kurt. Don't touch the pen. It's sticky.
Name. Flat. Time in. Time out.

steps.text: Then you were never here. Easier for everybody.

choices.text: Who else signed tonight? (Read the book.)

steps.text: There's nothing in here since... ninety-three.

super_hello.text: Twenty-seven! Up there. It smells like the way out.
Because I said so. The lift's dead and the stairs are... dirty. Second floor is dirty.

choices.text: Then help me fix the lift. You know the building.

steps.text: ...The fuses are upstairs, in the box by the lift. The breaker's in maintenance.

choices.text: The nameplate on your door says two names. Where's the other one?

steps.text: At her sister's. In Tula. She likes it there.
Women like to visit. Don't they?

choices.text: Then I'll make my own way up.
Get in my way again and I'll put you through that window.
The committee will want to see the lift for itself. I'll need the keys.

super_hello.text: Here. Maintenance. The breaker, the boiler. You bring that key back to me, and you don't go anywhere else with it.
And you stay out of my flat.
Off you go, then. I'll be here. I'm always here.
Go on. I'll know where you are. I always know where everybody is.
Go on, then, Kurt. It's a big building.
I don't like him. He smells like old soup. Old soup and something else.

super_found_in_flat.text: What are you doing in my home?
I told you. I was very clear.

super_found_out.text: The committee doesn't go through people's drawers.

super_sees_power.text: Who told you to touch my breaker?

socko_first_inhabitant.text: Ooh, a neighbour! She's busy. Busy people don't bite.

socko_listener.text: Shhh. That one can't see. It hears though. It hears REALLY good.
Crouch, buddy. Throw something. Noises go where you throw them.

socko_dark.text: Kurt, it's very dark in here and something is in the walls. Torch?

socko_fuse_hint.text: The box needs a fuse! Fuses are little. Little things hide in drawers.

socko_suggest_laundress.text: Kurt. Kurt. The big one's after the laundry lady.
Shut the door on them. He'll be busy for ages and we can go where we like.

socko_obeyed.text: See? Easy! You're good at this.

socko_suggest_bath.text: That's the one. It's holding the door shut, I can smell it.
It's just a big baby, Kurt. Big babies are the easiest kind.

socko_defied_2.text: Why are you making this hard?

socko_suggest_super.text: He's a bad man. You can tell. Bad men go bonk and then they're not bad any more.

socko_defied_3.text: Fine. Fine, fine, fine. Do it your way, Kurt. See where your way gets you.

wife_letter.text: From Tula. 'Lyuda, why don't you write.' Postmarked ninety-four.

wife_freezer.text: There's slippers. Why are there slippers by the freezer?
